summary: Pit titled 'Twin Carin Trees' at 2330 m, HS 112 cm, with no grain forms recorded: 0-35 cm 1F- to 4F+ gradient, a 1 cm 4F 'old crust' at 35-36 cm, 36-65 cm 4F- to 1F- gradient, F+ 65-79, a thin P layer at 79-80, soft F 80-104 and a 4F slab 104-112 cm flagged 'problematic layer' (CT1 SC at its base, 104 cm); no temperatures, aspect or slope
reading_issues: Hardness bars and boundaries (35, 36, 65, 79, 80, 104 cm) measured from pixels; boundaries fall on whole cm. Three layers are trapezoids (hardness gradients): 0-35 cm 1F- base to 4F+ top (mean 2.5, labelled 1F-), 36-65 cm 4F- base to 1F- top (mean 2.17, exact tie between 4F and 4F+, labelled 4F+). The grain-form/size/moisture table is entirely blank, so every layer has grain null and the only qualitative information is in the layer notes ('problematic layer' 112-104 cm, 'old crust' 36-35 cm). The red line at 104 cm marks the weak interface where CT1 SC occurred. Aspect, slope, wind and air temperature are blank in the header. Site title is spelled 'Twin Carin Trees' (Twin Cairns trees); the slug uses 'cairns'. Confidence medium because no grain information was recorded.
